📰 Patriots, Antennas, Fuel Tanks: Iran’s 4-Country “Response”

The Revolutionary Guards laid out the timeline like a press release: after Khamenei’s funeral ceremonies, the U.S. hit Iran’s southern coastal provinces and two bridges leading to Mashhad “to distract from the funeral.” 

Then came “the first stage of the response”: missiles and drones at four American-linked bases — Camp Arifjan and Ali Al Salem in Kuwait, and Al-Jufair and Sheikh Isa in Bahrain. The warning was simple: any further aggression will be met with “expanded” strikes.

Iran’s regular army, separate from the Guards and always eager to claim its own role, issued a different list: suicide drones on a Patriot air-defense battery in Kuwait, on a satellite warning antenna in Qatar, and on U.S. fuel tanks in Bahrain. 

The language stayed maximalist: the armed forces “will not under any circumstances allow the insane U.S. president to achieve his goals and ambitions” and “will defend the ideals of the Islamic Revolution until final victory.”

Bahrain’s defense ministry said it intercepted “several air attacks” and that forces were at peak defensive readiness. Kuwait reported one person wounded. In Qatar, civilians got a phone alert about “heightened security threat” and went on with their day. 

By midday, the fire shifted to Jordan: launches from Khomayn, Qom, Zanjan, Lorestan, Shiraz and Tehran toward the Muwaffaq Al-Salti base in Zarqa. 

The Guards claimed ten ballistic missiles at “the enemy’s command-and-control center in the Middle East” and the air base at Azraq, plus a promise that “other American bases in the region will not be safe from our heavy fire” if Washington hits again. 

Jordan’s military answered in three words: “We intercepted eight.”

Ten launched, eight intercepted, and nobody bothered to say clearly where the other two went. Amman’s airport delayed flights, the U.S. embassy told staff to shelter, an Ethiopian flight to Tel Aviv circled, and sirens in Jordan were heard in Israeli communities along the valley. 

In Iraq, alarms sounded in Baghdad and Erbil bases, intercepts were reported over Camp Victoria. Parallel to the “response against the superpower,” Iranian drones were sent at Iranian Kurdish opposition camps — proof that even under the banner of resistance to America, the regime finds time to shoot at other Iranians.

The head of Iran’s parliament national security committee wrapped it in one sentence: if the U.S. hits Iran’s national security again, “we will take their security anywhere they are.”
